verdict.summary: The lease/reclaim architecture and host boundary are sound, but schema/runtime drift, dual Python/Rust cores, unimplemented public policy fields, estimated native tokenization, and manual native packaging block a stable public API.

strengths: revocable borrowing requires a registered reclaim pipeline
request-transaction reclaim without background prompt mutation
no AINPC-specific dependency in the core

findings.title: Schema, Python enums, and Rust DTOs are different contracts
findings.impact: A schema-valid config can fail in Python or be silently ignored in Rust.
evidence: schema-valid values static/priority/semantic_pipeline/tool_schema/hybrid all raised ValueError in Python
Rust produced the same layout hash and allocations for fixed/weighted/priority/elastic
CLI validation accepts schema-forbidden unknown fields
findings.recommendation: Create one versioned contract, generate DTOs/enums, deny unknown fields, and add a schema corpus across Python and Rust.

findings.title: The advertised canonical Rust core is opt-in and feature-incomplete
findings.impact: Python and native consumers receive different behavior under the same version.
evidence: ContextLeaseArena is pure Python while NativeArena is a separate opt-in API
Python registers 14 algorithms; Rust implements four deterministic text algorithms plus semantic request orchestration
the Python wheel package-data contains no native library
findings.recommendation: Make the high-level Python API delegate to packaged native wheels and retain pure Python as an explicit reference/fallback implementation.

findings.title: Release metadata and default branch are not closed
findings.impact: Users can install or inspect a version that does not match the CLI or the complete implementation.
evidence: release verification does not inspect CLI version
local remote-tracking main is at fecb4ba while the reviewed implementation is on agent/rust-multilang-contextlease
findings.recommendation: Use one version source, add end-to-end version assertions, merge to main, then tag a prerelease.

findings.title: Public policy fields do not control behavior
findings.impact: allocation, lifecycle, reclaim, render_target, admission_policy and count_mode overstate the current runtime contract.
findings.recommendation: Implement a policy behavior matrix or remove/reserve unsupported fields until their semantics are testable.

findings.title: Native token accounting is estimated only
findings.impact: Hard context limits can be wrong for real provider serialization and tokenizers.
findings.recommendation: Add host tokenizer callbacks or measured-token inputs, canonical renderer counting, and actual-usage calibration.

findings.title: Prepared output loses structured message and tool semantics
findings.impact: Message roles, tool-call groups, schema structure, provenance and provider overhead cannot be represented faithfully.
findings.recommendation: Return a typed PreparedContextPlan and keep flat rendered text only as a convenience view.

findings.title: Semantic compression validation is too weak for production
findings.impact: Substring retention and monotonic size do not protect facts, negation, qualifiers, citations or tool protocol.
findings.recommendation: Add structured retention contracts, evidence/audit metadata, cache, deadlines, cancellation, cost limits and configurable portfolio selection.

findings.title: Cross-language conformance is too shallow
findings.impact: The current tests do not detect the contract and behavior drift observed in this review.
findings.recommendation: Add 20+ canonical fixtures, full Python-reference-to-Rust golden comparison, property tests, fuzzing and performance regression gates.

findings.title: Debug Web observability is Python-only
findings.impact: C++, Go, CSharp and direct Rust consumers cannot expose the same runtime view without a custom bridge.
findings.recommendation: Expose versioned content-free snapshots/events through the Rust ABI and optional OTLP/Prometheus exporters.

findings.title: Native installation requires manual assembly
findings.impact: Standard ecosystem installation does not produce a directly runnable native-backed client.
findings.recommendation: Ship platform Python wheels, NuGet RID assets, CMake/pkg-config packages and stable Go/native installation tooling.

findings.title: Performance gates are incomplete
findings.impact: Quadratic similarity compression, sequential portfolio calls, JSON FFI copies and serialized Python arena calls have no regression guard.
findings.recommendation: Add scale and concurrency benchmarks before introducing LSH, async portfolio, batching or ABI buffer improvements.

findings.title: Supply-chain and release trust are incomplete
findings.impact: Checksums alone do not provide artifact identity, provenance, dependency risk or ABI compatibility evidence.
findings.recommendation: Add pinned actions, security audits, SBOM, signing, SLSA provenance and ABI symbol compatibility tests.

python_readme_command.reason: src-layout package not installed or on PYTHONPATH

exit_criteria: async deadline cache and cost controls
fuzz benchmarks OTel SBOM and signing
